description: Technology detectors and Skills for the AIEF Adoption Engine. This is data, not workflow logic. Three distinct concepts: a DETECTOR fires on project signals (dependencies, files, keywords); a SKILL RECOMMENDATION maps fired detectors ('when') to a Skill; SKILL CONTENT (purpose, whenToUse, standardsToRead, promptContext, commonRisks, evidenceExpectations) is contextual knowledge injected into prompts — AIEF includes it as context, it does not execute Skills.

skills.name: Multitenant SaaS Architect
skills.description: Tenant isolation, Host header resolution, tenant lifecycle, SaaS architecture.
skills.whenToUse: Any Change that touches tenant resolution, tenant-scoped data or tenant lifecycle.
skills.promptContext: This is a multitenant system: every data access must be tenant-scoped, tenant resolution (e.g. by Host header or subdomain) is security-critical, and cross-tenant leakage is a critical bug.
commonRisks: queries missing the tenant filter
tenant resolution trusting client-provided values
shared caches leaking data across tenants
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state how tenant isolation was verified for anything touched.

skills.name: n8n Automation Ops
skills.description: n8n Queue Mode, workflow catalog, executions, workers, Redis, health checks.
skills.whenToUse: Changes that call the n8n API, manage workflows/executions, or affect automation reliability.
skills.promptContext: n8n is an external system: calls to its API must handle timeouts and failures explicitly, workflow activation is a privileged operation, and executions carry potentially sensitive payloads.
commonRisks: treating n8n as always available
activating workflows without human approval
logging execution payloads with sensitive data
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should record how n8n interactions were tested (mock or real instance).

skills.name: AWS SaaS Platform
skills.description: Cognito, RDS PostgreSQL, Secrets Manager, CloudFront, WAF, CloudWatch, CodePipeline, Terraform.
skills.whenToUse: Changes involving AWS services, authentication flows or infrastructure configuration.
skills.promptContext: AWS-managed services are configured, not reimplemented: validate tokens server-side (e.g. Cognito JWTs), read secrets from the environment/secret manager, and treat infrastructure changes as reviewable code.
commonRisks: validating JWTs client-side only
hardcoding region/pool identifiers
IAM permissions broader than needed
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should note which AWS interactions were exercised for real vs mocked.

skills.name: Security & RBAC Reviewer
skills.description: Server-side authorization, permissions, tenant isolation, secrets, audit events.
skills.whenToUse: Any Change touching authentication, authorization, permissions or sensitive data.
skills.promptContext: Authorization is enforced server-side on every operation; the UI is never a security boundary. Check permissions at the point of data access, not only at the route entry.
commonRisks: authorization checked in the UI but not the API
new endpoints missing permission checks
secrets or tokens ending up in logs or evidence files
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should list which permission paths were tested, including a denied-access case.

skills.name: Next.js / NestJS Architecture
skills.description: Frontend/backend separation, server components, APIs, NestJS modules, adapter patterns.
skills.whenToUse: Changes that cross the frontend/backend boundary or add routes, server components or modules.
skills.promptContext: Keep the server/client boundary explicit: secrets and privileged calls stay server-side, client components receive plain serializable props, and API contracts are validated at the boundary.
commonRisks: server-only code or secrets imported into client bundles
data fetching duplicated on both sides of the boundary
API responses without input validation
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state how the affected routes/components were exercised.

skills.name: AI Workflow Governance
skills.description: AI-generated workflows, human approval, inactive drafts, governance, auditability.
skills.whenToUse: Changes where AI generates or modifies artifacts that affect runtime behavior.
skills.promptContext: AI-generated artifacts start inactive and require human approval before affecting runtime; every generation/approval should be attributable and auditable.
commonRisks: auto-activating generated artifacts
no record of who approved what
prompts or outputs containing secrets
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should show the approval path for anything AI-generated.

skills.name: Graphify / AST Architecture Understanding
skills.description: Hybrid code-graph understanding: Graphify's Gemini-enriched semantic graph when available, static AST reading otherwise.
skills.whenToUse: Understand/Plan phases of a Change that needs the repository's architecture or dependency topology, or when graphify-out/ already exists.
skills.promptContext: Build architecture/dependency understanding with a hybrid rule: if GEMINI_API_KEY is available to you, use the Graphify Skill to produce the enriched semantic graph; if it is not, read the codebase statically (imports, module boundaries, call sites) to build the same understanding offline, at $0. Either way, persist findings under graphify-out/ (already gitignored — never a hidden .aief/ directory, ADR-009) and summarize the result in knowledge/architecture-graph.md.
commonRisks: treating the static fallback as lower-confidence without saying so in evidence
AIEF's own CLI never calls Gemini or holds the API key — that stays entirely on the assistant side
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state which mode was used (semantic or static) and where the resulting summary was written.

skills.name: Python Backend Architecture
skills.description: Django/Flask/FastAPI: input validation at the boundary, async/blocking-call safety, settings and secret hygiene.
skills.whenToUse: Changes that add or modify routes/views, models, background tasks, or settings in a Django, Flask or FastAPI project.
skills.promptContext: Validate all external input at the boundary (serializers/schemas, not raw request dicts), never run blocking synchronous I/O inside an async handler (FastAPI's async def, Django's async views), and keep secrets and DEBUG flags out of settings.py/config — read them from the environment.
commonRisks: raw SQL string interpolation instead of the ORM or parameterized queries
DEBUG=True or a hardcoded SECRET_KEY reaching a production settings file
blocking synchronous I/O (a sync DB driver, requests.get) inside an async endpoint, stalling the event loop for every other request
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state how the affected routes/views were exercised and confirm DEBUG/secret settings were not touched or exposed.

skills.name: Payments & Billing Reviewer
skills.description: Stripe/payment integration: idempotency, webhooks, PCI scope, refunds.
skills.whenToUse: Any Change that touches payment processing, subscriptions, webhooks, or stored payment methods.
skills.promptContext: Payment operations must be idempotent (use idempotency keys), webhook handlers must verify signatures before trusting payloads, and no raw card data should ever touch AIEF-managed code (use Stripe Elements/hosted fields to stay out of PCI scope).
commonRisks: webhook handler trusting payload without signature verification
double-charging from a retried request with no idempotency key
storing raw card numbers or CVV anywhere in logs or the database
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state how webhook signature verification and idempotency were exercised (real Stripe test mode or mocked).

skills.name: Container & Deployment Reviewer
skills.description: Docker/Kubernetes: image hardening, secrets handling, resource limits, rollout safety.
skills.whenToUse: Changes that add or modify a Dockerfile, docker-compose service, or Kubernetes/Helm manifest.
skills.promptContext: Container images should run as a non-root user, never bake secrets into image layers, and Kubernetes manifests should declare resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness probes so a bad rollout fails safely.
commonRisks: secrets committed into a Dockerfile ARG/ENV or an image layer
container running as root by default
a Deployment with no resource limits or health probes, letting one bad pod exhaust a node
skills.evidenceExpectations: Evidence should state how the image/manifest change was validated (local build, dry-run apply, or a real cluster).

skills.name: Project Architecture Reviewer
skills.description: General architecture review, module boundaries, risks, and technical debt.
skills.whenToUse: When no specific technology signals are detected and a general review is the safest starting point.
